newsitem.title: USA: Travelers Property upbeat on earnings.
newsitem.headline: Travelers Property upbeat on earnings.

text.p: Travelers Property Casualty Corp. said Monday it expects sustained earnings growth partly because of its success in cutting costs since it bought Aetna Inc's property-casualty business last year.

"We're pretty positive on our ability to grow shareholder value and grow profitability of the company," Travelers Property Casualty Chief Financial Officer William Hannon told Reuters in an interview.
He declined to give specific projections.
Hannon said Travelers was ahead of schedule in trimming 3,300 jobs since the $4 billion Aetna acquisition last April.
The 3,300 job cuts will be completed by the middle of this year, or about six months ahead of the original schedule, Hannon said.
The "vast bulk" of these job cuts have come through attrition, a Travelers Property Casualty spokesman said.
The company had 23,000 U.S. employees when it was formed a year ago, when parent Travelers Group bought the Aetna operation for $4 billion.
"We're going to keep the lid on very tight on expenses, to the extent that that helps us continue to do well," Hannon said.

Hannon said the company was fast approaching its goal of $300 million in annualized expense savings, announced last year after the Aetna acquisition. He said that lease costs, as the two formerly separate entities combined their operations, would account for up to $80 million of that savings.

He also said the company expected solid growth from its personal lines business. "It's growing up," he said. "It's not an adult yet, but it's not an infant anymore, either. That's an opportunity for us to grow." He said the sector was helped by agents from sister company Primerica Financial Services, whose agents sell auto and homeowners insurance for Travelers.

But Hannon said the commercial lines market remained tough. "Pricing is very competitive. In terms of getting new premiums, I don't think you should be looking for us to do a lot of that, because... the margins are so low, that in a lot of cases it doesn't strike us as a good deal."
Hannon said Travelers is interested in buying rival property casualty operations but that no acquisitions are in the works at the moment.
Travelers Property Casualty is an 82 percent owned subsidiary of Travelers Group.
